newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ex-c.bank chief sees Turkey inflation at 100 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ex-c.bank chief sees Turkey inflation at 100 pct.

text.p: Former central bank governor and opposition member of parliament Rusdu Saracoglu said on Friday that Turkey's inflation would be at best 100 percent for 1997.
"If the government does not make a big mistake, inflation will be about 100 percent this year," Saracoglu told a news conference.
Saracoglu, who was central bank governor for six years to 1993, said the Islamist-conservative coalition government was not taking serious measures against Turkey's economic problems.

"I do not expect a crisis unless a mistake is made," he said. Saracoglu resigned in a rift with then prime minister and now foreign minister Tansu Ciller just ahead of a financial crisis in 1994 that sent interest rates high into three digits and led to the devaluation of the lira.
"But I expect the budget deficit to be between 2,500 trillion and 2,750 trillion lira," said Saracoglu, who is now a member of the main opposition Motherland Party.
Saracoglu said the government manipulated numbers and graphs to give a falsely optimistic picture of the economy.
"They are trying to create a fantasy budget that is balanced or even in the black," he said.
The government has announced it will produce a balanced budget in 1997 following a 1,200 trillion lira deficit in 1996.

Saracoglu said the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, which is expected to visit Turkey next month amid speculation of a deal with Ankara, would begin to doubt Turkey's other targets, including its projected 236 trillion lira tax earnings for this year.
"With this lack of seriousness, a deal does not appear possible," Saracoglu said.
